Kingsbury began to play with Arcade Fire in 2003 after the break-up of the band's original membership.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Although Kingsbury primarily plays bass in Arcade Fire, he also plays guitar and sings.[[7]](#cite_note-:4-7)

The U.S. states of [Ohio](/wiki/Ohio "Ohio") and [North Carolina](/wiki/North_Carolina "North Carolina") both take credit for the Wright brothers and their world-changing inventions—Ohio because the brothers developed and designed their plane in [Dayton](/wiki/Dayton,_Ohio "Dayton, Ohio"), and North Carolina because [Kitty Hawk](/wiki/Kitty_Hawk,_North_Carolina "Kitty Hawk, North Carolina") was the site of the Wrights' first powered flight. Polonium :: History :: chunk_0010
Tentatively called "[radium F](/wiki/Radium#History "Radium")", polonium was discovered by [Marie](/wiki/Marie_Curie "Marie Curie") and Pierre Curie in July 1898,[[38]](#cite_note-c1-38)[[39]](#cite_note-39) and was named after Marie Curie's native land of [Poland](/wiki/Poland "Poland") ([Latin](/wiki/Latin_language "Latin language"): *Polonia*).[[40]](#cite_note-40)[[41]](#cite_note-41) Poland at the time was under [Russian](/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire"), [German](/wiki/German_Empire "German Empire"), and [Austro-Hungarian](/wiki/Austro-Hungarian_Empire "Austro-Hungarian Empire") [partition](/wiki/Partitions_of_Poland "Partitions of Poland"), and did not exist as an independent country. It was Curie's hope that naming the element after her native land would publicize its lack of independence. Polonium may be the first element named to highlight a political controversy.[[42]](#cite_note-Przemysl-42)

This element was the first one discovered by the Curies while they were investigating the cause of [pitchblende](/wiki/Uraninite "Uraninite") [radioactivity](/wiki/Radioactivity "Radioactivity"). Pitchblende, after removal of the radioactive elements [uranium](/wiki/Uranium "Uranium") and [thorium](/wiki/Thorium "Thorium"), was more radioactive than the uranium and thorium combined. This spurred the Curies to search for additional radioactive elements. They first separated out polonium from pitchblende in July 1898, and five months later, also isolated [radium](/wiki/Radium "Radium").[[18]](#cite_note-nbb-18)[[38]](#cite_note-c1-38)[[43]](#cite_note-c2-43) German scientist [Willy Marckwald](/wiki/Willy_Marckwald "Willy Marckwald") successfully isolated 3 milligrams of polonium in 1902, though at the time he believed it was a new element, which he dubbed "radio-tellurium", and it was not until 1905 that it was demonstrated to be the same as polonium.[[44]](#cite_note-44)[[45]](#cite_note-45)

Mamet is the daughter of American playwright, essayist, screenwriter, and film director [David Mamet](/wiki/David_Mamet "David Mamet") and actress [Lindsay Crouse](/wiki/Lindsay_Crouse "Lindsay Crouse"). Her father is the grandson of Polish Jews[[6]](#cite_note-tt-6) and she says her given name is Polish and Russian.[[7]](#cite_note-7) Her maternal grandfather was playwright [Russel Crouse](/wiki/Russel_Crouse "Russel Crouse") and her maternal great-grandfather was educator [John Erskine](/wiki/John_Erskine_(educator) "John Erskine (educator)"). She has a sister, Willa, who is a singer, and two half-siblings: [Clara](/wiki/Clara_Mamet "Clara Mamet"), also an actress and director; and Noah. She lived in New England until age five when her mother moved to [Pacific Palisades, California](/wiki/Pacific_Palisades,_California "Pacific Palisades, California"), with Willa and Zosia.[[8]](#cite_note-nyt1-8) After finishing high school, Mamet decided to pursue acting instead of going to college.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

In 2012, Mamet was cast by [Judd Apatow](/wiki/Judd_Apatow "Judd Apatow") in the [HBO](/wiki/HBO "HBO") series *[Girls](/wiki/Girls_(TV_series) "Girls (TV series)")*. She has subsequently appeared as a regular in television series such as *[The Flight Attendant](/wiki/The_Flight_Attendant "The Flight Attendant")*, *[The Decameron](/wiki/The_Decameron_(TV_series) "The Decameron (TV series)")*, and *[Laid](/wiki/Laid_(American_TV_series) "Laid (American TV series)")*.

Italian campaign (World War II) :: Campaign :: Invasion of Sicily :: chunk_0007
Main article: [Allied invasion of Sicily](/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Sicily "Allied invasion of Sicily")

The initial plan was for landings in the south-east, south and north-west areas of the island which would lead to the rapid capture of key Axis airfields and except for [Messina](/wiki/Messina "Messina"), all the main ports on the island. This would allow a rapid Allied build-up, as well as denying their use to the Axis.[[49]](#cite_note-62) This was altered into a reduced number of landings but with more concentration of force.

The Allied invasion of [Sicily](/wiki/Sicily "Sicily"), Operation Husky, began on 9 July 1943 with both amphibious and airborne landings at the [Gulf of Gela](/wiki/Gela "Gela"). The land forces involved were the [U.S. Seventh Army](/wiki/Seventh_United_States_Army "Seventh United States Army"), under [Lieutenant General](/wiki/Lieutenant_general_(United_States) "Lieutenant general (United States)") [George S. Patton](/wiki/George_S._Patton "George S. Patton"), the 1st Canadian Infantry Division and the 1st Canadian Armoured Brigade under the command of Major-General [Guy Simonds](/wiki/Guy_Simonds "Guy Simonds") and the [British Eighth Army](/wiki/Eighth_Army_(United_Kingdom) "Eighth Army (United Kingdom)"), under [General](/wiki/General_(United_Kingdom) "General (United Kingdom)") [Bernard Montgomery](/wiki/Bernard_Montgomery "Bernard Montgomery").

The original plan required a strong advance by the British northwards along the east coast to Messina. The Canadians took the central position, with the British on their right and the Americans on the left. The Canadian War Cemetery in Agira is testament to the sacrifice made driving the Germans from the rugged terrain. Main article: [Harvard University endowment](/wiki/Harvard_University_endowment "Harvard University endowment")

Harvard has the largest [university endowment](/wiki/List_of_colleges_and_universities_in_the_United_States_by_endowment "List of colleges and universities in the United States by endowment") in the world, valued at about $50.7 billion as of 2023.[[20]](#cite_note-BGendow-20)[[21]](#cite_note-HFRendow-21)

During the [recession of 2007–2009](/wiki/Great_Recession "Great Recession"), it suffered significant losses that forced large budget cuts, in particular temporarily halting construction on the Allston Science Complex.[[98]](#cite_note-99) The endowment has since recovered.[[99]](#cite_note-100)[[100]](#cite_note-101)[[101]](#cite_note-102)[[102]](#cite_note-103)

About $2 billion of investment income is annually distributed to fund operations.[[103]](#cite_note-104)
Harvard's ability to fund its degree and financial aid programs depends on the performance of its endowment; a poor performance in fiscal year 2016 forced a 4.4% cut in the number of graduate students funded by the [Faculty of Arts and Sciences](/wiki/Harvard_Faculty_of_Arts_and_Sciences "Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences").[[104]](#cite_note-105)
Endowment income is critical, as only 22% of revenue is from students' tuition, fees, room, and board.[[105]](#cite_note-106)

**Sweden**,[[f]](#cite_note-15) formally the **Kingdom of Sweden**,[[g]](#cite_note-17)[[h]](#cite_note-18) is a [Nordic country](/wiki/Nordic_countries "Nordic countries") located on the [Scandinavian Peninsula](/wiki/Scandinavian_Peninsula "Scandinavian Peninsula") in [Northern Europe](/wiki/Northern_Europe "Northern Europe"). It borders [Norway](/wiki/Norway "Norway") to the west and north, and [Finland](/wiki/Finland "Finland") to the east, and shares a maritime border with [Denmark](/wiki/Denmark "Denmark") to the south. At 450,295 square kilometres (173,860 sq mi),[[4]](#cite_note-auto-7) Sweden is the largest Nordic country by both area and population, and is the [fifth-largest country in Europe](/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_area "List of European countries by area"). Its capital and largest city is [Stockholm](/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm"). Sweden has a population of 10.6 million, and a low population density of 25.5 inhabitants per square kilometre (66/sq mi); 88% of [Swedes](/wiki/Swedes "Swedes") reside in urban areas.[[11]](#cite_note-SCBdensity2020-19) They are mostly in the central and southern half of the country. Sweden's urban areas together cover 1.5% of its land area. Sweden has a diverse [climate](/wiki/Climate_of_Sweden "Climate of Sweden") owing to the length of the country, which ranges from [55°N](/wiki/55th_parallel_north "55th parallel north") to [69°N](/wiki/69th_parallel_north "69th parallel north").

Both sexual and asexual means are used to increase the number of plants; seeds and multiplication of corms are the most common means of production, but [tissue culture](/wiki/Plant_tissue_culture "Plant tissue culture") can be used,[[114]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERana2021-116) most commonly for saffron crocus. New corms are formed on top of the older corm which withers away, and cormels are produced from axillary buds.[[112]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDe_Hertogh_et_al201281-114) The production of new plants begins with harvested corms in late June to early July, after being graded by corm size the corms are stored around 22 °C (72 °F) until early October when they are moved to 17 °C (63 °F) until planted later in October and November; flowering occurs in March and the flowers are not removed. Crocuses are also forced to produce flowering plants out of season and the most common species used are *C. vernus* and *C. flavus*, and most of the corms used for forcing come from the Netherlands.[[115]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDe_Hertogh1992-117)

Spring flowering types are planted in fall, while fall-blooming types in late summer; typically, the corms are placed 3 to 4 inches (7.6 to 10.2 cm) deep in well-draining soil in areas with full sun exposure. They do not thrive in heavy clay soils or those that are damp, especially during their summer dormancy period.[[116]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTETenenbaum2003-118) Commercial crops are produced on raised beds and slopes, to ensure adequate drainage, while horticulturalists often plant on sand beds for the same purpose.[[117]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERuksans201120-119) Spring flowering types also do well in areas with deciduous trees, where they flower and produce leaves before the trees completely leaf-out. [Orcus](/wiki/Orcus_(dwarf_planet) "Orcus (dwarf planet)"), [Quaoar](/wiki/Quaoar "Quaoar"), [Gonggong](/wiki/Gonggong_(dwarf_planet) "Gonggong (dwarf planet)"), and [Sedna](/wiki/Sedna_(dwarf_planet) "Sedna (dwarf planet)") are generally agreed to be dwarf planets among astronomers, and all but Sedna are known to have moons.[[10]](#cite_note-IAU-C8812-10) A number of other smaller objects, such as [Huya](/wiki/38628_Huya "38628 Huya"), [Salacia](/wiki/120347_Salacia "120347 Salacia"), [Uni](/wiki/55637_Uni "55637 Uni"), [Varda](/wiki/174567_Varda "174567 Varda"), and [Chiminigagua](/wiki/532037_Chiminigagua "532037 Chiminigagua"), also have moons, although their dwarf planethood is more doubtful.

As of November 2025, 471 [asteroid moons](/wiki/List_of_asteroid_moons "List of asteroid moons") and 149 [trans-Neptunian moons](/wiki/Minor-planet_moon#Trans-Neptunian_objects "Minor-planet moon") (including those of Pluto and the other dwarf planets) had been discovered.[[11]](#cite_note-Johnstonsarchive-list-11)

Monaco :: Demographics :: Language :: chunk_0026
Main article: [Languages of Monaco](/wiki/Languages_of_Monaco "Languages of Monaco")

The main and official language of Monaco is [French](/wiki/French_language "French language"), while [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language") is spoken by the principality's sizeable community from Italy. French and Italian are in fact more spoken in the principality today than [Monégasque](/wiki/Mon%C3%A9gasque_dialect "Monégasque dialect"), its historic vernacular language. A variety of [Ligurian](/wiki/Ligurian_(Romance_language) "Ligurian (Romance language)"), Monégasque is not recognised as an official language; nevertheless, some signage appears in both French and Monégasque, and the language is taught in schools. English is also used.

Italian was the official language in Monaco until 1860, when it was replaced by French.[[37]](#cite_note-miglioverde-40) This was due to the annexation of the surrounding [County of Nice](/wiki/County_of_Nice "County of Nice") to France following the [Treaty of Turin (1860)](/wiki/Treaty_of_Turin_(1860) "Treaty of Turin (1860)").[[37]](#cite_note-miglioverde-40)

The [Grimaldi](/wiki/Grimaldi_Family "Grimaldi Family"), [princes of Monaco](/wiki/Princes_of_Monaco "Princes of Monaco"), are of Ligurian origin; thus, the traditional national language is [Monégasque](/wiki/Mon%C3%A9gasque_language "Monégasque language"), a variety of [Ligurian](/wiki/Ligurian_(Romance_language) "Ligurian (Romance language)"), now spoken by only a minority of residents and as a common second language by many native residents. In [Monaco-Ville](/wiki/Monaco-Ville "Monaco-Ville"), street signs are printed in both French and Monégasque.[[188]](#cite_note-197)[[189]](#cite_note-198)
